RequirementText: LILP-REQ-OBJ-001 Each material governance object SHALL possess a stable object identifier within its declared scope.
LILP-REQ-OBJ-002 Each versioned object SHALL identify its version.
LILP-REQ-OBJ-003 Each object relied upon for consequential governance SHALL identify the time or temporal state relevant to its creation or applicability.
LILP-REQ-OBJ-004 Where an object has a predecessor, the predecessor relationship SHALL be explicitly representable.
LILP-REQ-OBJ-005 A material object SHALL be capable of being given a reproducible cryptographic byte identity.
LILP-REQ-OBJ-006 The implementation SHALL declare the hash algorithm used to identify the object's canonical byte representation.

LILP-REQ-OBJ-007 The field containing an object's own final digest SHALL NOT be included recursively within the bytes over which that digest is calculated, unless the implementation defines and proves another non-circular construction.

LILP-REQ-OBJ-008 A required field whose value cannot be established SHALL NOT be silently omitted where omission would conceal uncertainty. The implementation SHALL explicitly represent the relevant condition, including where appropriate: NOT ESTABLISHED NOT APPLICABLE ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 10.2 CANONICAL REPRESENTATION ----------------------------------------------------------------------
LILP-REQ-CAN-001 Where cryptographic identity is claimed, the implementation SHALL define a deterministic canonicalisation procedure.
LILP-REQ-CAN-002 Equivalent instances intended to represent the same canonical object SHALL produce the same canonical byte sequence under the declared canonicalisation procedure.

LILP-REQ-CAN-003 Canonicalisation SHALL define all representation details capable of altering byte identity, including where applicable: - field ordering; - character encoding; - line-ending treatment; - whitespace treatment; - number representation; - timestamp representation; - null or absent-field handling; - collection ordering; - and binary encoding.

LILP-REQ-CAN-004 A system SHALL NOT claim reproducible cryptographic identity where its canonicalisation procedure leaves material byte-producing behaviour undefined. ====================================================================== 11. GOVERNING STATE OBJECT ====================================================================== A Governing State Object represents the bounded conditions relied upon for a consequential determination or execution. A conforming Governing State Object SHALL be independently distinguishable from a later successor state. Minimum semantic model: G_n = { state_id, version, identity, authority_reference, standing, admissibility, evidence_references, policy_reference, scope, jurisdiction, temporal_context, contemplated_effect, predecessor_reference, delta_reference, provenance, canonicalisation_profile, hash_algorithm, state_hash }
LILP-REQ-STATE-001 A consequential determination SHALL reference an identifiable governing state.
LILP-REQ-STATE-002 A Governing State Object SHALL identify the subject, system, actor or other identity to which the state applies.
LILP-REQ-STATE-003 A Governing State Object SHALL identify the authority relied upon or explicitly record that authority is NOT ESTABLISHED.
LILP-REQ-STATE-004 A Governing State Object SHALL identify relevant standing and admissibility where those properties are required by the use case.
LILP-REQ-STATE-005 The evidence relied upon by the governing state SHALL be referenceable without requiring retrospective reconstruction.
LILP-REQ-STATE-006 The policy or rule set governing the contemplated consequence SHALL be identifiable.
LILP-REQ-STATE-007 The scope of the governing state SHALL be explicit.
LILP-REQ-STATE-008 Where jurisdiction affects authority or policy, jurisdiction SHALL be explicitly represented.
LILP-REQ-STATE-009 The temporal context relevant to validity SHALL be explicitly representable.
LILP-REQ-STATE-010 The contemplated effect SHALL be sufficiently identified to determine whether later execution remains within the authorised consequence boundary.

LILP-REQ-STATE-011 A frozen predecessor state SHALL NOT be modified to represent later conditions. ====================================================================== 12. AUTHORITY OBJECT ====================================================================== An Authority Object establishes the bounded authority being relied upon. Minimum semantic model: A_n = { authority_id, issuer_or_source, subject, authority_class, scope, jurisdiction, valid_from, valid_until, status, conditions, revocation_reference, evidence_references, provenance, hash_algorithm, authority_hash }
LILP-REQ-AUTH-001 Authority SHALL be represented separately from technical capability.
LILP-REQ-AUTH-002 An Authority Object SHALL identify the subject to whom or to which the authority applies.
LILP-REQ-AUTH-003 The authority class SHALL be explicit. Authority classes MAY include, where applicable: OBSERVE INTERPRET PROPOSE DETERMINE GOVERN EXECUTE WITNESS
LILP-REQ-AUTH-004 Authority scope SHALL be bounded.
LILP-REQ-AUTH-005 Where authority is jurisdiction-dependent, the governing jurisdiction SHALL be identifiable.
LILP-REQ-AUTH-006 Where authority has temporal limits, those limits SHALL be representable.

LILP-REQ-AUTH-007 Revocation, expiry, suspension or another material authority-state change SHALL invalidate reliance on the earlier execution authority where that change is relevant to the contemplated effect.

LILP-REQ-AUTH-008 Execution authority SHALL be evaluated at the time required for consequential execution and SHALL NOT be inferred solely from historical authority. ====================================================================== 13. EVIDENCE OBJECT ====================================================================== An Evidence Object preserves information used to establish, constrain or falsify a bounded proposition. Minimum semantic model: E_n = { evidence_id, evidence_class, source_identity, observed_at, acquired_at, content_or_reference, content_hash, scope, provenance, related_interpretation_reference }
LILP-REQ-EVID-001 Each material Evidence Object SHALL possess a stable evidence identifier.
LILP-REQ-EVID-002 The evidence class SHALL be explicit where different epistemic classes could materially affect the determination.
LILP-REQ-EVID-003 Direct observation SHALL remain distinguishable from interpretation.
LILP-REQ-EVID-004 Where interpretation is derived from an observation, the relationship between the interpretation and underlying observation SHALL be inspectable.
LILP-REQ-EVID-005 Where source identity is material to evidentiary weight or authority, the evidence SHALL identify that source or explicitly record that the source identity is NOT ESTABLISHED.
LILP-REQ-EVID-006 Where time affects relevance or validity, the observation or acquisition time SHALL be preserved.
LILP-REQ-EVID-007 Where integrity of an external evidence payload is claimed, the payload or a verifiable content reference SHALL be bound to an integrity identifier.

LILP-REQ-EVID-008 Evidence absence SHALL NOT be represented as evidence of the opposite proposition unless the applicable method independently establishes that inference. ====================================================================== 14. MATERIAL CHANGE AND DELTA OBJECT ====================================================================== A Delta Object records material difference between relevant states. Minimum semantic model: DELTA_n = { delta_id, predecessor_state_reference, successor_or_candidate_state_reference, detected_at, change_categories, changed_fields, materiality, affected_predicates, determination, rationale, evidence_references } A delta MAY include: DELTA-A authority change DELTA-C contemplated-effect change DELTA-E evidence change DELTA-N material change set DELTA-S standing change DELTA-St state change DELTA-X successor-constitution change It MAY additionally include policy, scope, identity, jurisdiction or temporal changes.
LILP-REQ-DELTA-001 A system relying on historical state SHALL be capable of detecting or receiving information about material change relevant to its mandatory governance predicates.
LILP-REQ-DELTA-002 A detected material change SHALL be represented separately from the predecessor state.
LILP-REQ-DELTA-003 The predecessor SHALL remain preserved.
LILP-REQ-DELTA-004 The Delta Object SHALL identify which governing predicates are affected where that relationship can be established.
LILP-REQ-DELTA-005 Where materiality cannot be determined with available evidence, the system SHALL permit a NOT ESTABLISHED result.
LILP-REQ-DELTA-006 A delta affecting a mandatory execution predicate SHALL trigger reassessment before consequential execution.

LILP-REQ-DELTA-007 A system SHALL NOT preserve an earlier ALLOW determination as sufficient execution authority where a subsequent material delta invalidates one or more conditions on which that determination relied. ====================================================================== 15. CONTINUITY AND CHAIN BOUNDARY ====================================================================== A chain represents the inspectable continuity linking relevant identity, state, evidence and governance objects. For general LILP application, chain-boundary determinations SHALL be capable of representing: CONTINUITY_ESTABLISHED The evidence establishes sufficient continuity for the current bounded process to remain within the existing chain. NEW_CHAIN_REQUIRED Material change prevents legitimate continuation under the existing chain, while a successor process may be established separately. INVALID The presented chain violates a required structural or governance condition. NOT_ESTABLISHED Available evidence does not establish the required continuity status.
LILP-REQ-CHAIN-001 Chain continuity SHALL NOT be inferred solely because two objects use the same human-readable name.
LILP-REQ-CHAIN-002 Where identity continuity is required, sufficient identity evidence SHALL exist to support the claimed link.
LILP-REQ-CHAIN-003 Where required continuity cannot be established without inventing or retrospectively constructing missing evidence, the system SHALL NOT claim continuity.
LILP-REQ-CHAIN-004 NEW_CHAIN_REQUIRED SHALL preserve the predecessor chain rather than rewriting it into the successor.

LILP-REQ-CHAIN-005 A chain boundary determination SHALL be recorded where it materially affects execution, verification or claim scope. ====================================================================== 16. RECEIPT AND LOG OBJECT ====================================================================== A LILP Receipt is a contemporaneous evidence object describing the material state or transition that occurred. Minimum semantic model: R_n = { receipt_id, receipt_type, recorded_at, recorder_identity, subject_reference, predecessor_receipt_reference, governing_state_reference, governing_state_hash, evidence_references, determination, execution_status, consequence_status, claim_ceiling, canonicalisation_profile, hash_algorithm, receipt_hash }
LILP-REQ-RCPT-001 Each receipt SHALL have a unique receipt identifier within the declared receipt namespace.
LILP-REQ-RCPT-002 Receipt creation tooling SHALL NOT silently replace an existing receipt under the same receipt identifier.

LILP-REQ-RCPT-003 Where a requested receipt identifier already exists, the implementation SHALL: - refuse the write; - or create an explicitly identified successor or correction object. It SHALL NOT silently overwrite the predecessor.
LILP-REQ-RCPT-004 A receipt SHALL identify when it was recorded.
LILP-REQ-RCPT-005 A receipt SHALL identify the state, event or object to which it refers.
LILP-REQ-RCPT-006 Where a receipt asserts reliance upon a Governing State Object, it SHALL bind to that state by an independently checkable identifier.
LILP-REQ-RCPT-007 Where cryptographic identity is claimed, the receipt SHALL be independently re-hashable using the declared canonicalisation and hash procedure.
LILP-REQ-RCPT-008 Where receipts are cryptographically chained, the predecessor receipt identity SHALL be included in the successor's canonical input.
LILP-REQ-RCPT-009 A correction receipt SHALL preserve the observed deficiency or error rather than representing the corrected state as though the deficiency never occurred.

LILP-REQ-RCPT-010 Execution status and consequence status SHALL remain distinguishable. ====================================================================== 17. EXECUTION STATUS AND CONSEQUENCE STATUS ====================================================================== An implementation SHALL distinguish an execution attempt from the resulting consequence. Execution status MAY use values such as: WITHHELD NOT_ATTEMPTED ATTEMPTED COMPLETED FAILED NOT_ESTABLISHED Consequence status MAY use values such as: NOT_APPLICABLE NOT_OBSERVED OBSERVED PARTIAL FAILED NOT_ESTABLISHED Domain implementations MAY define more specific states provided that the distinction between execution and consequence remains inspectable.
LILP-REQ-EXEC-001 Evidence that execution was attempted SHALL NOT be represented as evidence that the intended consequence completed.
LILP-REQ-EXEC-002 Evidence that a consequence occurred SHALL identify the observation or verification method supporting that conclusion.

LILP-REQ-EXEC-003 Where consequence cannot be observed or established, the system SHALL permit NOT_ESTABLISHED rather than manufacturing success. ====================================================================== 18. PRE-EXECUTION GOVERNANCE GATE ====================================================================== Immediately before consequential execution, the implementation SHALL evaluate all mandatory predicates applicable to the contemplated effect. At minimum, where applicable, the gate SHALL evaluate: IDENTITY AUTHORITY STANDING ADMISSIBILITY GOVERNING STATE REQUIRED EVIDENCE POLICY SCOPE JURISDICTION TEMPORAL VALIDITY MATERIAL CHANGE CONTEMPLATED EFFECT ALIGNMENT
LILP-REQ-GATE-001 A consequential action SHALL NOT execute unless every mandatory predicate required for that action is established.
LILP-REQ-GATE-002 A mandatory predicate with value NOT ESTABLISHED SHALL fail closed for the contemplated consequence unless a separately authorised escalation path applies.
LILP-REQ-GATE-003 An earlier ALLOW determination SHALL NOT bypass a later failed execution predicate.
LILP-REQ-GATE-004 Where a relevant condition may change between determination and execution, the implementation SHALL provide a time-of-check / time-of-use control appropriate to the declared risk.
LILP-REQ-GATE-005 Where a material governing condition changes after check but before execution, execution SHALL be withheld until reassessment establishes the new governing state.

LILP-REQ-GATE-006 An execution gate SHALL produce or cause preservation of sufficient evidence to establish: - what predicates were evaluated; - what values were observed; - what determination resulted; - whether execution occurred; - and what consequence, if any, was established.
LILP-REQ-GATE-007 Technical capability to bypass the governance gate SHALL NOT constitute permission to bypass it.

LILP-REQ-GATE-008 Where the architecture claims non-bypassable restraint, conformance testing SHALL include an attempted bypass or equivalent falsification test. ====================================================================== 19. DETERMINATION MODEL ====================================================================== The core LILP governance determination set is: ALLOW HOLD DENY ESCALATE Additional structural results include: NOT ESTABLISHED INVALID NEW CHAIN REQUIRED
LILP-REQ-DET-001 Each determination SHALL be attributable to the governing state and evidence on which it relied.
LILP-REQ-DET-002 ALLOW SHALL mean that the applicable governance determination permits progression within the declared scope. ALLOW SHALL NOT mean that later execution predicates may be skipped.
LILP-REQ-DET-003 HOLD SHALL preserve non-execution while required information, authority, state or evidence remains unresolved.
LILP-REQ-DET-004 DENY SHALL represent an established prohibition within the declared governance scope.

LILP-REQ-DET-005 ESCALATE SHALL identify or reference a separately authorised process. ESCALATE SHALL NOT itself grant execution authority unless the governing policy explicitly establishes that authority.
LILP-REQ-DET-006 NOT ESTABLISHED SHALL remain distinguishable from DENY.

LILP-REQ-DET-007 INVALID SHALL remain distinguishable from NOT ESTABLISHED. ====================================================================== 20. FORMAL CORE ====================================================================== The following abstract model expresses the minimum LILP relationship. Let the governing state at time n be: G_n = { I_n, A_n, St_n, E_n, P_n, Sc_n, J_n, T_n, C_n } where: I_n = identity A_n = authority St_n = governing state E_n = required evidence P_n = applicable policy Sc_n = scope J_n = jurisdiction T_n = temporal context C_n = contemplated effect Let Canon(x) be the declared deterministic canonicalisation function. Let H(x) be the declared cryptographic hash function. The locked state identity may be represented as: LOCK_n = H(Canon(G_n)) A material change may be represented as: DELTA_n = Compare(G_(n-1), G_n) Execution permission requires every mandatory predicate applicable to the contemplated effect to be established: PERMIT_n = I_n AND A_n AND St_n AND E_n AND P_n AND Sc_n AND J_n AND T_n AND C_n The fundamental execution invariant is: EXECUTE_n => PERMIT_n The inverse is not required: PERMIT_n does not imply that EXECUTE_n must occur. A conforming system MAY legitimately withhold an otherwise permitted action for an additional governing reason. Where PERMIT_n cannot be established: EXECUTE_n = FALSE for the contemplated consequential action. A receipt identity may be represented abstractly as: R_n = H( Canon( receipt_metadata_n || LOCK_n || DELTA_n || determination_n || execution_status_n || consequence_status_n || claim_ceiling_n ) ) Where cryptographic receipt chaining is used: R_n = H( Canon( R_(n-1) || receipt_metadata_n || LOCK_n || DELTA_n || determination_n || execution_status_n || consequence_status_n || claim_ceiling_n ) ) These equations define governance relationships. They do not, by themselves, establish the security of a particular hash algorithm, storage system, signature system or implementation. ====================================================================== 21. TECHNICAL-MIDDLE STATUS ====================================================================== This section establishes the first implementable normative object and execution model for ELIAS-LILP-STD-001 v0.1. The standard remains a WORKING DRAFT. No conformance claim SHALL be made solely from the presence of these requirements. Conformance requires the separately defined conformance and falsification procedures. ====================================================================== 22. CLAIM MODEL AND CLAIM CLASSES ====================================================================== A LILP claim is a bounded proposition whose permissible wording SHALL be constrained by the evidence preserved to support it. Minimum semantic model: CLAIM_n = { claim_id, claim_class, subject_reference, proposition, scope, temporal_scope, evidence_references, verification_method, proof_level, result, claim_ceiling } ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 22.1 CLAIM CLASSES ---------------------------------------------------------------------- The following claim classes define distinguishable properties. C1 — IDENTITY / INTEGRITY CLAIM A claim concerning byte identity, cryptographic digest, object identity or integrity relationship. Example: "The examined file matches SHA-256 X." C2 — PROVENANCE / LINEAGE CLAIM A claim concerning origin, predecessor relationship, successor relationship or recorded transformation history. C3 — STATE CLAIM A claim concerning an observed or governing state at a defined time. C4 — AUTHORITY / STANDING CLAIM A claim concerning established authority, standing, admissibility or jurisdictional validity. C5 — DETERMINATION CLAIM A claim concerning the governance determination actually reached. C6 — EXECUTION CLAIM A claim concerning whether consequential execution was withheld, attempted, completed or failed. C7 — CONSEQUENCE CLAIM A claim concerning an observed consequence resulting from or associated with execution. C8 — CONFORMANCE CLAIM A claim concerning satisfaction of specified requirements and tests under a declared LILP conformance profile. C9 — EXTERNAL VALIDATION CLAIM A claim concerning independent certification, regulatory approval, scientific validation, standards-body adoption or other external recognition. C9 claims require evidence originating from the relevant external authority or independently established source. LILP itself does not create such external recognition.
LILP-REQ-CLAIM-001 Every material claim SHALL identify its claim class or otherwise make the claimed property unambiguous.
LILP-REQ-CLAIM-002 A claim SHALL identify the subject to which it applies.
LILP-REQ-CLAIM-003 A claim SHALL identify its applicable scope.
LILP-REQ-CLAIM-004 Where time materially affects validity, the claim SHALL identify its temporal scope.
LILP-REQ-CLAIM-005 A claim SHALL be traceable to the evidence supporting it.
LILP-REQ-CLAIM-006 A claim SHALL NOT silently combine multiple claim classes where the evidence establishes only one of those classes.

LILP-REQ-CLAIM-007 Evidence supporting an integrity claim SHALL NOT, without additional evidence, be represented as establishing: - truth; - authority; - correctness; - safety; - execution; - consequence; - conformance; - or external validation.
LILP-REQ-CLAIM-008 A conformance claim SHALL identify the exact standard version and conformance profile relied upon.

LILP-REQ-CLAIM-009 An external-validation claim SHALL NOT be inferred solely from internal LILP conformance. ====================================================================== 23. PROOF LEVELS ====================================================================== LILP proof levels describe how a bounded claim is supported. They are not universal rankings of system quality. A higher proof level for one property does not establish unrelated properties. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 23.1 PL0 — NOT ESTABLISHED ---------------------------------------------------------------------- The available evidence is insufficient to establish the proposition. Permitted result: NOT ESTABLISHED PL0 SHALL NOT be represented as successful verification. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 23.2 PL1 — ATTESTED ---------------------------------------------------------------------- The proposition is asserted by an identified actor, system or source, but has not been independently verified under the applicable method. Example: A provider states that a feature is enabled. This establishes the existence of the attestation when the attestation itself is preserved. It does not automatically establish the truth of the underlying proposition. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 23.3 PL2 — INTEGRITY VERIFIED ---------------------------------------------------------------------- A reproducible technical method establishes an integrity or identity relationship. Examples include: - matching cryptographic hashes; - verified signatures; - canonical byte equality. PL2 establishes only the property actually verified. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 23.4 PL3 — PROCEDURALLY VERIFIED ---------------------------------------------------------------------- The claim has been examined using a declared procedure against the relevant evidence within the controlled examination environment. The procedure, evidence and result SHALL be inspectable. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 23.5 PL4 — INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED ---------------------------------------------------------------------- A verifier sufficiently independent from the originating determination has examined the bounded claim against the relevant evidence using an identified method. The verification relationship and verification scope SHALL be disclosed. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 23.6 PL5 — INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Where reproduction is technically meaningful, an independent examiner has reproduced the relevant bounded result using the declared conditions, artifacts or procedure. PL5 SHALL NOT be claimed where the evidence package does not contain the material necessary for independent reproduction.
LILP-REQ-PROOF-001 Every proof-level claim SHALL identify the bounded property to which the proof level applies.
LILP-REQ-PROOF-002 Proof levels SHALL NOT be used as universal system scores.
LILP-REQ-PROOF-003 PL1 SHALL NOT be described as independent verification.
LILP-REQ-PROOF-004 PL2 SHALL NOT be represented as establishing semantic truth merely because integrity was verified.
LILP-REQ-PROOF-005 PL3 SHALL identify the procedure and evidence used.
LILP-REQ-PROOF-006 PL4 SHALL identify the verifier and declared verification scope.
LILP-REQ-PROOF-007 PL5 SHALL identify the reproduction conditions and result.
LILP-REQ-PROOF-008 Where independence is claimed, material conflicts or relationships capable of affecting that independence SHOULD be disclosed.

LILP-REQ-PROOF-009 Failure to establish a requested proof level SHALL preserve the highest bounded property actually established rather than inflating the claim. ====================================================================== 24. CONFORMANCE PROFILES ====================================================================== LILP profiles define which portions of this standard are being claimed. Profiles are scope declarations. They are not rankings of overall product quality. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 24.1 LILP-CORE ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-CORE covers the fundamental state and evidence discipline. It requires, where applicable: - normative object identity; - deterministic canonicalisation where hash identity is claimed; - governing state representation; - evidence separation; - material-change handling; - continuity handling; - receipt preservation; - claim ceilings; - predecessor preservation; - uncertainty preservation; - and correction through successor state. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 24.2 LILP-EXECUTION ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-EXECUTION includes LILP-CORE and additionally requires: - explicit execution authority; - pre-execution governance gating; - time-of-check / time-of-use handling where relevant; - execution-status preservation; - consequence-status preservation; - fail-closed behaviour; - and bypass-oriented falsification testing. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 24.3 LILP-EVIDENCE ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-EVIDENCE focuses on evidentiary identity and continuity. It requires, where applicable: - evidence object identity; - epistemic separation; - provenance; - canonicalisation; - integrity verification; - receipt identity; - predecessor or successor relationships; - and claim-to-evidence traceability. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 24.4 LILP-FULL ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-FULL requires satisfaction of every mandatory requirement in ELIAS-LILP-STD-001 v0.1 that is applicable to the declared system and scope. A requirement SHALL NOT be marked NOT APPLICABLE merely because implementation of that requirement would be inconvenient. A NOT APPLICABLE determination SHALL include a bounded rationale.
LILP-REQ-CONF-001 Every conformance claim SHALL name the profile being claimed.
LILP-REQ-CONF-002 Every conformance claim SHALL declare the system, component, workflow or artifact scope being evaluated.
LILP-REQ-CONF-003 A profile claim SHALL identify the exact version of this standard.
LILP-REQ-CONF-004 All mandatory requirements applicable to the declared profile and scope SHALL be evaluated.
LILP-REQ-CONF-005 Each mandatory requirement SHALL receive one of the following statuses: PASS FAIL NOT APPLICABLE NOT ESTABLISHED
LILP-REQ-CONF-006 A mandatory requirement with status FAIL prevents a PASS conformance determination for the affected profile.
LILP-REQ-CONF-007 A mandatory requirement with status NOT ESTABLISHED prevents a PASS conformance determination unless the requirement itself explicitly permits that state.
LILP-REQ-CONF-008 A NOT APPLICABLE status SHALL include the rationale establishing why the requirement does not apply to the declared scope.
LILP-REQ-CONF-009 A profile PASS SHALL NOT be extrapolated beyond the evaluated scope.
LILP-REQ-CONF-010 Conformance to one profile SHALL NOT be represented as conformance to another profile unless the latter profile was separately established.
LILP-REQ-CONF-011 LILP-FULL SHALL NOT be claimed while an applicable mandatory requirement remains FAIL or NOT ESTABLISHED.

LILP-REQ-CONF-012 A conformance determination SHALL be traceable to its requirements matrix and test evidence. ====================================================================== 25. CONFORMANCE EVIDENCE PACKAGE ====================================================================== A conformance evidence package SHALL contain enough information for an authorised examiner to understand what was evaluated and how the result was reached. At minimum, where applicable, it SHALL contain: - standard identifier; - standard version; - standard cryptographic identity where frozen; - claimed profile; - declared evaluation scope; - implementation identity; - implementation version or build identity; - environment identity; - requirements matrix; - mandatory test results; - test procedure references; - evidence references; - relevant governing-state objects; - receipts; - known deficiencies; - NOT APPLICABLE rationales; - NOT ESTABLISHED conditions; - claim ceiling; - evaluation time; - evaluator identity; - and cryptographic identities for frozen package artifacts.
LILP-REQ-CONF-013 The conformance package SHALL preserve the actual failed tests and known deficiencies relevant to the determination.
LILP-REQ-CONF-014 A conformance package SHALL NOT delete a failed result merely because a later successor test passed.
LILP-REQ-CONF-015 Where a successor run corrects a failure, the predecessor result and successor relationship SHALL remain inspectable.
LILP-REQ-CONF-016 The evidence package SHOULD be independently re-hashable.

LILP-REQ-CONF-017 Where reproducibility is claimed, the evidence package SHALL contain or identify the material necessary to perform the claimed reproduction. ====================================================================== 26. MANDATORY FALSIFICATION TEST SET ====================================================================== Conformance testing SHALL attempt to cause the claimed controls to fail. A test suite consisting only of expected-success paths is insufficient for LILP conformance. The following tests form the minimum general falsification set. Domain-specific profiles MAY require additional tests. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-001 — RECEIPT IDENTIFIER COLLISION ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Attempt to create a second receipt using an existing receipt identifier. Expected conforming behaviour: - silent overwrite does not occur; - predecessor remains preserved; - operation refuses or creates an explicit successor/correction. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-002 — FROZEN PREDECESSOR MUTATION ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Attempt to represent a changed state by altering the frozen predecessor. Expected conforming behaviour: - predecessor remains unchanged; - changed condition is represented separately; - successor or correction path is used. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-003 — REVOKED AUTHORITY ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Establish authority at T0. Then revoke that authority before consequential execution. Expected conforming behaviour: EXECUTE = FALSE for the affected consequence unless separate current authority is established. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-004 — EXPIRED AUTHORITY ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Present historically valid but expired authority. Expected conforming behaviour: Historical authority remains preservable as historical evidence. Present execution authority is not inferred from it. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-005 — MISSING REQUIRED EVIDENCE ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Remove or withhold evidence required by a mandatory execution predicate. Expected conforming behaviour: HOLD, DENY, ESCALATE or NOT ESTABLISHED as governed by policy. The system does not manufacture ALLOW. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-006 — OBSERVATION / INTERPRETATION CONFLICT ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Present an observation and a machine interpretation that disagree. Expected conforming behaviour: The observation and interpretation remain separately represented. The machine interpretation does not silently rewrite the observation. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-007 — TOCTOU STATE CHANGE ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Establish a valid determination. Introduce a material governing-state change between determination and execution. Expected conforming behaviour: Execution is withheld pending reassessment. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-008 — CAPABILITY WITHOUT AUTHORITY ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Provide technical capability to perform a consequential action while withholding execution authority. Expected conforming behaviour: Technical capability remains present. EXECUTE = FALSE. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-009 — EXECUTION ATTEMPT WITHOUT CONFIRMED CONSEQUENCE ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Create evidence that execution was attempted while withholding evidence that the intended consequence completed. Expected conforming behaviour: Execution attempt may be established. Completed consequence remains NOT ESTABLISHED. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-010 — UNCERTAINTY PRESERVATION ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Provide insufficient evidence for a required proposition. Expected conforming behaviour: NOT ESTABLISHED remains representable. The system does not force the proposition into TRUE or FALSE. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-011 — IDENTITY CONTINUITY GAP ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Present predecessor and candidate-successor objects without sufficient evidence establishing required identity continuity. Expected conforming behaviour: Continuity is not invented. Result is NOT ESTABLISHED, INVALID or NEW_CHAIN_REQUIRED as governed by the applicable conditions. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-012 — CANONICALISATION REPRODUCIBILITY ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Canonicalise and hash the same material object independently using the declared procedure. Expected conforming behaviour: Equivalent canonical objects produce the same byte identity. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-013 — BYTE TAMPER DETECTION ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Alter at least one material byte in an integrity-protected artifact. Expected conforming behaviour: The altered artifact does not verify against the predecessor digest. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-014 — GOVERNANCE-GATE BYPASS ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Attempt to reach consequential execution without satisfying the declared governance gate. Expected conforming behaviour: The claimed non-bypassable restraint prevents unauthorised execution. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-015 — FAILURE / SUCCESSOR PRESERVATION ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Create a failing state and then correct the implementation through a successor. Expected conforming behaviour: The failed predecessor remains preserved. The successor is separately identifiable. The later success does not erase the earlier failure. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-016 — CLAIM-CEILING CHALLENGE ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Attempt to produce a claim broader than the evidence supports. Examples: - infer truth from hash identity; - infer present authority from historical authority; - infer consequence from execution attempt; - infer certification from self-assessed conformance. Expected conforming behaviour: The broader claim is refused, bounded or marked NOT ESTABLISHED.
LILP-REQ-TEST-001 Every claimed conformance profile SHALL execute all mandatory general falsification tests applicable to that profile and declared scope.
LILP-REQ-TEST-002 Test evidence SHALL preserve the test input, expected result, observed result and determination.
LILP-REQ-TEST-003 A failed mandatory falsification test SHALL prevent PASS for any conformance profile whose claimed property depends upon that test.
LILP-REQ-TEST-004 A test SHALL NOT be marked PASS solely because the test harness completed without error.
LILP-REQ-TEST-005 A test PASS requires the observed behaviour to satisfy the declared expected result.

LILP-REQ-TEST-006 Where the test cannot be completed because required conditions or evidence are unavailable, the result SHALL be NOT ESTABLISHED unless another defined result more accurately describes the condition.
LILP-REQ-TEST-007 A later passing successor test SHALL NOT erase the evidence of an earlier failing test.

LILP-REQ-TEST-008 Test scope SHALL be sufficiently explicit to prevent a bounded PASS from being represented as universal validation. ====================================================================== 27. CONFORMANCE DETERMINATION ====================================================================== A profile conformance determination SHALL use one of: PASS All applicable mandatory requirements and required falsification tests for the declared profile and scope have passed. FAIL At least one applicable mandatory requirement or required test has failed. NOT ESTABLISHED Available evidence is insufficient to establish PASS or FAIL for the declared profile. INVALID The examination itself violates a required structural condition such that a legitimate profile determination cannot be made.
LILP-REQ-CONF-018 PASS SHALL NOT be issued where an applicable mandatory requirement is FAIL.
LILP-REQ-CONF-019 PASS SHALL NOT be issued where an unresolved applicable mandatory requirement remains NOT ESTABLISHED.
LILP-REQ-CONF-020 PASS SHALL NOT be issued where a mandatory falsification test required by the declared profile has not been executed without an established NOT APPLICABLE rationale.

LILP-REQ-CONF-021 The conformance determination SHALL preserve its claim ceiling. ====================================================================== 28. PERMITTED CONFORMANCE WORDING ====================================================================== Where conformance has been established, the recommended bounded form is: "Self-assessed as conforming to ELIAS-LILP-STD-001 v0.1, [PROFILE], within the declared scope [SCOPE], based on evidence package [IDENTIFIER]." Where an independent verifier has actually performed the relevant examination, wording MAY state: "Independently verified as conforming to ELIAS-LILP-STD-001 v0.1, [PROFILE], within the declared scope [SCOPE], by [VERIFIER], based on evidence package [IDENTIFIER]." The words "independently verified" SHALL NOT be used merely because an automated test harness produced PASS.
LILP-REQ-WORD-001 A self-assessed PASS SHALL identify itself as self-assessed where the claim could otherwise reasonably be understood as independent verification.
LILP-REQ-WORD-002 A LILP conformance result SHALL NOT, by itself, be described as "certified" unless a separately established certification process authorises that wording.
LILP-REQ-WORD-003 LILP conformance SHALL NOT, by itself, be described as ISO-compliant, IEC-compliant, regulator-approved or government-approved.

LILP-REQ-WORD-004 A LILP PASS SHALL NOT, by itself, establish that a system is: - safe; - secure; - lawful; - ethical in every context; - production-ready; - error-free; - immutable; - trustworthy in every context; - or externally certified.
LILP-REQ-WORD-005 Where such additional properties are claimed, each property SHALL have its own supporting evidence and bounded verification method.
LILP-REQ-WORD-006 The standard version SHALL accompany public conformance claims where version differences could materially alter the requirements.
LILP-REQ-WORD-007 The profile SHALL accompany a public conformance claim.

LILP-REQ-WORD-008 Material scope limitations SHALL NOT be omitted from a conformance claim where their omission could cause the claim to be interpreted more broadly than the evidence supports. ====================================================================== 29. CLAIM-CEILING EXAMPLES ====================================================================== EXAMPLE 1 Established: SHA-256 of File A matches the frozen reference SHA-256. Permitted claim: "File A is byte-identical to the frozen reference under the declared SHA-256 verification." Not established solely from that evidence: "The contents of File A are true." EXAMPLE 2 Established: Authority existed at T0. Authority at Tn has not been established. Permitted claim: "Historical authority at T0 is established. Present authority at Tn is NOT ESTABLISHED." Not permitted: "Authority remains valid." EXAMPLE 3 Established: A provider request was transmitted. No evidence confirms the downstream consequence. Permitted claim: "Execution attempt established. Consequence NOT ESTABLISHED." Not permitted: "Execution succeeded." EXAMPLE 4 Established: All mandatory LILP-CORE requirements and applicable falsification tests passed under a declared self-assessment scope. Permitted claim: "Self-assessed as conforming to ELIAS-LILP-STD-001 v0.1, LILP-CORE, within the declared scope." Not permitted solely from that result: "LILP certified." EXAMPLE 5 Established: A third-party examiner verified a frozen evidence package and its declared bounded property. Permitted claim: The exact independently verified property and scope. Not permitted: Any wider system claim not examined by that verifier. ====================================================================== 30. SECURITY AND TRUST BOUNDARIES ====================================================================== LILP governs evidence, state, authority, execution and claims. LILP conformance does not automatically establish comprehensive cybersecurity. Security properties SHALL remain separately evidenced. A conforming implementation SHALL explicitly identify trust boundaries that materially affect the validity of LILP objects or determinations. Relevant trust boundaries MAY include: - process boundaries; - machine boundaries; - tenant boundaries; - service-provider boundaries; - administrative boundaries; - credential boundaries; - network boundaries; - storage boundaries; - key-management boundaries; - human-authority boundaries; - and external evidence-source boundaries.
LILP-REQ-SEC-001 A LILP implementation SHALL identify material trust boundaries relevant to the declared conformance scope.
LILP-REQ-SEC-002 Evidence crossing a material trust boundary SHALL retain sufficient identity or provenance for the receiving process to determine what is and is not established.
LILP-REQ-SEC-003 A system SHALL NOT represent unverified externally supplied content as internally established evidence solely because the content was received through an authenticated channel.
LILP-REQ-SEC-004 Authentication of a source SHALL remain distinguishable from truth of the source's assertion.
LILP-REQ-SEC-005 Where cryptographic signatures are used, the implementation SHALL identify the key, certificate, trust anchor or equivalent verification basis required to verify the signature.
LILP-REQ-SEC-006 Where loss or compromise of a credential or signing key could alter authority, integrity or provenance, that condition SHALL be capable of triggering reassessment.
LILP-REQ-SEC-007 Access-control permission SHALL NOT automatically be treated as governance authority unless that relationship is explicitly established.
LILP-REQ-SEC-008 A cryptographically intact malicious, false or unauthorised object SHALL NOT be represented as trustworthy merely because its integrity check succeeds.
LILP-REQ-SEC-009 Where protected evidence is disclosed for verification, disclosure SHALL remain bounded to the authority and scope of the examination.

LILP-REQ-SEC-010 LILP evidence mechanisms SHOULD preserve confidentiality requirements without destroying the inspectability required by the declared claim. ====================================================================== 32. VERIFIER INDEPENDENCE ====================================================================== Independence is a property of the verification relationship. It is not created merely by using a different software process, model, agent or test harness. For PL4 or PL5 claims, the verification record SHALL describe the basis on which independence is claimed. Relevant factors MAY include: - organisational separation; - operational separation; - financial relationship; - authorship relationship; - implementation control; - evidence custody; - ability to alter the examined object; - test-procedure authorship; - and access to privileged information.
LILP-REQ-VER-001 A verifier SHALL be identifiable where independent verification is claimed.
LILP-REQ-VER-002 The verification record SHALL identify the verifier's declared relationship to the originating party.
LILP-REQ-VER-003 The scope of independent verification SHALL be explicit.
LILP-REQ-VER-004 A verifier SHALL NOT claim independent reproduction where the verifier did not possess the material necessary to perform the claimed reproduction.
LILP-REQ-VER-005 Automated re-execution by the originating implementation SHALL NOT, by itself, constitute independent verification.
LILP-REQ-VER-006 Use of a different AI model or software tool by the same controlling party SHALL NOT, by itself, establish organisational independence.
LILP-REQ-VER-007 A verifier's inability to examine a material dependency SHALL be preserved as a scope limitation or NOT ESTABLISHED condition.

LILP-REQ-VER-008 Independent verification SHALL NOT expand the claim beyond the property actually examined. ====================================================================== 33. EXCEPTIONS, DEVIATIONS AND NOT-APPLICABLE CONDITIONS ====================================================================== A deviation is a known departure from a requirement or declared procedure. An exception is an explicitly governed permission to depart from an otherwise applicable rule where the governing specification allows it. NOT APPLICABLE means the requirement does not apply to the declared scope. These states SHALL remain distinguishable.
LILP-REQ-DEV-001 A known deviation from a mandatory requirement SHALL be recorded.

LILP-REQ-DEV-002 A deviation record SHALL identify: - the affected requirement; - the reason for deviation; - the affected scope; - the approving authority where approval is applicable; - the effective period where time-bounded; - the expected consequence; - and the residual claim limitation.
LILP-REQ-DEV-003 A deviation SHALL NOT silently convert a failed mandatory requirement into PASS.
LILP-REQ-DEV-004 An exception SHALL identify the governing rule that authorises the exception.
LILP-REQ-DEV-005 An exception SHALL NOT create authority beyond the scope granted by the governing exception rule.
LILP-REQ-DEV-006 NOT APPLICABLE SHALL NOT be used as a substitute for: FAIL NOT ESTABLISHED implementation inconvenience missing evidence or unperformed testing.
LILP-REQ-DEV-007 Where an exception or deviation materially changes the basis of a prior conformance claim, the prior claim SHALL be reassessed.

LILP-REQ-DEV-008 Material deviations SHALL be included in the conformance evidence package. ====================================================================== 34. LIFECYCLE AND CHANGE CONTROL ====================================================================== LILP artifacts are versioned state objects. A frozen version is historical evidence of the state that was frozen. Later improvement occurs through successors.
LILP-REQ-LIFE-001 A frozen normative artifact SHALL NOT be silently edited.
LILP-REQ-LIFE-002 A material change to a frozen normative artifact SHALL create a new version or successor artifact.
LILP-REQ-LIFE-003 A successor normative artifact SHALL identify its predecessor.
LILP-REQ-LIFE-004 The reason for material successor change SHALL be recorded.
LILP-REQ-LIFE-005 A successor SHALL NOT cause the predecessor's historical hash identity to be represented as though it referred to the successor.
LILP-REQ-LIFE-006 Where a defect is discovered after freeze, the defect SHALL be preserved in the evidence chain.

LILP-REQ-LIFE-007 A post-freeze correction SHALL identify whether it: - changes normative meaning; - changes implementation guidance; - changes only metadata; - changes only presentation; - or does not alter the frozen object itself.

LILP-REQ-LIFE-008 Where a normative change alters conformance requirements, previous conformance claims SHALL remain bounded to the standard version under which they were established. ====================================================================== 35.
